newsitem.title: JAPAN: Minor Metals - Asian markets seen relatively quiet.
newsitem.headline: Minor Metals - Asian markets seen relatively quiet.

text.p: Minor metals markets in Asia are expected to be relatively quiet this week, with cobalt likely to stay that way until after the U.S. Defense Logistics Agency's (DLA) sales tender closes in early December, Japanese traders said on Tuesday.
Traders in Hong Kong and China also said markets there were quiet with no big rush for any particular metal.
Cobalt ingots of 99.3 percent were heard offered at $20.80 per pound, CIF Hong Kong from Europe, and traders were said offering 99.5 percent at $21.80 per pound.
"They see the market firming and are asking a slightly higher price," said one Hong Kong-based trader.
Japanese traders said the bullish sentiment remained intact from last week, and high-grade cobalt was currently being quoted at over $22 a lb on a CIF Europe basis.
Tokyo traders said they expected cobalt prices to stay at current levels until the DLA accepts bids for cobalt stockpile sales in early December.
"The market will attract buying after the DLA sales," a cobalt trader in Tokyo said.

In the molybdenum market, a trader who just returned from Istanbul said that during his stay he had sold 200 tonnes of molybdenum oxide at $4.05 per pound on a CIF Europe basis and ferro-molybdenum at $9.55 per kilo, also on a CIF Europe basis.
A ferro-alloys conference was held in Istanbul last week.
Japanese traders said molybdenum oxide prices would remain firm in the next two to three months. "Molybdenum prices have been bullish since last week," a trader said.
Antimony was said to firm, with some bids for antimony high oxide heard at $2,100/$2,100.50 per tonne, CIF the United States.
"Of course all business concluded was below $2,000 per tonne," said the Chinese trader based in Hong Kong, without providing details.
The ferro-tungsten market continued dropping, but business was done last week with a few containers sold at $5.10/$5.20 kg, on a CIF Hong Kong basis, an industry source said.

For tungsten, Chinese suppliers could not compete with Russia, according to one Hong Kong-based trader who said Russian offers were "well below $5.00 per kg". -- Mishi Saran, Hong Kong News Desk +85-2-2843-6358 -- Eiichiro Tokumoto, Tokyo Commodity Desk +81-3-3432-7391
